_readme: THE BLOCKING SAMPLED REVIEW LEDGER. scripts/inventory-coverage.py --check READS
this file and blocks the next batch when the previous one has no recorded
sample, was reviewed by a non-fresh reviewer, or scored below 80%.
⛔ THIS IS A GATE, NOT A PROCESS STEP. Plan B had the sampled review as a
process step with no mechanism, and this repo record is that process steps
decay and mechanisms do not. A ledger CI does not read is a process step
⛔ WHY THE REVIEWER MUST BE FRESH-CONTEXT. A reviewer who authored the batch
rubber-stamps their own summary. `reviewer_context` must read `fresh`, and
recording it as fresh when it was not is the one lie this whole mechanism
cannot detect — which is exactly why it is written down rather than assumed.
RUBRIC, one yes/no per sampled entry:
Would a competent RavenClaude user learn something they could NOT have
guessed from the title plus the 200-character summary?
SAMPLE: 25% stratified across artifact classes, minimum 3.

batches.reviewer: fresh-context subagents (general-purpose), one per sampled entry, dispatched 2026-08-20
batches.status: REVIEWED — round 1 scored 67% and BLOCKED; reworked; round 2 scored 100%
note: ⛔ THIS BATCH IS DELIBERATELY BLOCKED, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING.
The wave-1 entries were authored by the same session that built the gate.
Recording that session as a fresh-context reviewer would be precisely the
self-review this ledger exists to prevent, so `reviewer_context` reads
therefore BLOCKS, which is the designed end state for wave 1 — the plan
says so directly: the nuance bar is not machine-checkable end to end, and
there is a required human/fresh-model step that IS the real gate.
TO CLEAR IT: a reviewer with no memory of the authoring session grades the
three sampled entries against the rubric above, then sets `reviewer`,
`reviewer_context: fresh`, and the three `verdicts`. At or above 80% the
gate opens; below it, wave 1 is reworked before wave 2 may begin.
⛔ check-nuance-floor.py --golden names, every run, which adversarial
negatives cleared the deterministic floor UNCAUGHT. Those are caught only
here. This step is not ceremony.
sample_rationale: hook-message-channels — the largest covers[] (47 hooks) and the owner own
worked example, so a restatement here would be the most expensive one.
must-fail-conventions-diverge — the script class, tier: effect.
hook-emitter-collision — a tier: none entry, so the sample includes one
whose honesty rests entirely on its written rationale.
reviewer_method: Three INDEPENDENT reviewers, one per sampled entry, so no cross-entry anchoring.
Each received ONLY the title, the 200-char summary, the nuance text, and the
one-question rubric. No advocacy, no authoring rationale, no indication of who
wrote them or that they were expected to pass.
⛔ The plan contemplates a 'human/fresh-model step' (§20-4). These are fresh
MODEL reviewers, not humans, and the record says so rather than implying a

verdict_reasons.hook-message-channels: Names the exact delivered fields, the exit-0 qualifier, and that stderr fails on every event. (confidence 0.85)
verdict_reasons.must-fail-conventions-diverge: The inverted DIRECTION (0 means teeth-passed in one tool, teeth-FAILED in the other), not merely the fact of divergence, is unguessable from the summary. (confidence 0.62)
verdict_reasons.hook-emitter-collision: The summary withholds the answer; the entry supplies a per-field asymmetry (concat vs replace) and the silent-discard consequence, contradicting the natural assumption that hooks on one event chain or behave uniformly. (confidence 0.65)

outcome: ⛔ BOTH ROUNDS STAY RECORDED. A ledger that keeps only the passing round proves
nothing — the whole value of this mechanism is that it caught a real authoring
defect on a batch that had already cleared the deterministic floor.
What it caught: a 200-char summary that STATED THE FINDING, leaving the nuance
nothing to teach. The floor structurally cannot see that — a leaky summary makes
the nuance's tokens LESS novel against baseline B1, so it pushes the entry toward
FAILING F2, not passing it. This class is reachable only by the sampled review.
The reusable rule is now in docs/best-practices/inventory-authoring.md §3 rule 6.

reasons.hook-message-channels: Names the exact delivered fields, the exit-0 qualifier, and that stderr fails on every event. (confidence 0.85)
reasons.must-fail-conventions-diverge: The inverted DIRECTION (0 means teeth-passed in one tool, teeth-FAILED in the other), not merely the fact of divergence, is unguessable from the summary. (confidence 0.62)
reasons.hook-emitter-collision: ⛔ REJECTED: the SUMMARY already states 'one channel adds, the other overwrites' — the entry only supplies the two channel names, whose semantics a competent reader infers from the names alone. (confidence 0.72)

review_rounds.outcome: BLOCKED. hook-emitter-collision rejected: its 200-char summary stated the finding, so the nuance had nothing left to teach.

review_rounds.reviewer: a NEW fresh-context subagent, no memory of round 1
reworked: hook-emitter-collision — summary rewritten as a tooltip; the nuance text is UNCHANGED

reasons.hook-emitter-collision: The summary withholds the answer; the entry supplies a per-field asymmetry (concat vs replace) and the silent-discard consequence, contradicting the natural assumption that hooks on one event chain or behave uniformly. (confidence 0.65)

review_rounds.outcome: PASSES. ⛔ The ENTRY was repaired, never the grade — the nuance text is byte-identical to the round-1 version that failed. What changed is the summary that was leaking it.
